text: The Shanti Vun Meditation Garden The Shanti Vun Meditation Garden (or Peace Forest) is a lovely, tranquil spot established at Landis Arboretum in 2019. Thanks to support from Landis friend Vijaya Luxmi and the efforts of dedicated volunteers, the Garden took shape during the pandemic years of 2020 and 2021 and continues to be developed. Vijaya Luxmi wanted to create Shanti Vun in memory of her father, Darshan Lal, and mother, Kamla Devi. The various trees honor the memories of her close friends and relatives, all now dancing in the winds of Landis Arboretum and Shanti Vun Meditation Garden. Visitors can enjoy the musical notes of the waterfall in the garden pond or sit at a picnic table in the covered Pavilion for lunch or just to relax and enjoy the view. The existing meditation labyrinth has been renewed, and in a few short years, the newly installed birch grove will be mature. Already, visitors are finding the garden a joyful place to be. During fine weather, the Garden becomes home to at 7:00 PM each first and third Thursday of the month. When you come to enjoy this peaceful spot, please refrain from dropping anything into the pond; do not feed the fish (it isn’t healthy for them) or toss pebbles into the water. For your own safety and for the structural integrity of the pond, do not climb on the rocks surrounding the pond or the waterfall. If you visit with your well-behaved, leashed dog, remember to clean up and dispose of any “gifts” they may leave so the area remains pleasant for everyone. text: Whether it's skiing, hiking, biking or fishing, any outdoor activity is nearby when you are in Boulder. Before you begin your next adventure, you need to have the proper gear. Luckily, downtown Boulder has you covered with a curated outdoor gear guide that will help you find your equipment needs from the East End to the West End of our downtown district! View All Sporting Goods Spots Rapha Boulder, located at the east end of Pearl Street, offers near-instant access to some of the country’s best riding along with fine coffee, race viewings, events, and the full range of Rapha clothing and accessories. No matter the season, Patagonia has you covered. Patagonia's breathable shirts, pants and shorts are not only stylish, but eco-friendly as well. On the other hand, it is hard to be much warmer on the mountain with their toasty ski jackets, snow-pants, down jackets and layers. You also can not go wrong with their wide variety of backpacks and duffle-bags that are perfect for your next backpacking trip or flight. MontBell on the East End has a tremendous selection of hiking, camping and climbing gear. They have plenty of backpacks, tents and camping accessories to complete any camping adventure, as well as lightweight and breathable clothes that are perfect for your next hike! Head to Black Diamond for backpacking, climbing and skiing needs. They specializes in climbing gear and carry everything from harnesses, rappel devices, carabiners, shoes, backpacks and more. They also make amazing backcountry ski gear from beacons, probes, packs and bindings, not to mention gear for the less extreme skiers such as jackets, gloves and snow-pants. Pedestrian Shops is the stop for the proper shoes to guide you on your future outdoor experiences. Check out their hiking or athletic shoes that are made for being outside in Boulder. Pedestrian Shops also has a variety of hiking socks that are a necessity for when you are on the trail! HIMALI creates premium mountaineering apparel and gives back to the Nepali community. Founded off the spirit of adventure, this gear equips anyone journeying into the wild. Head to Helly Hansen for stylish skiing equipment. Check out their ski jackets and snow-pants that are extremely warm and will surely keep you comfortable all winter long! They also have a great selection of durable backpacks that are awesome for any activity. Stride Lab focuses on natural footwear and foot health- our shoes are foot-shaped and zero-drop. We carry brands like Vivobarefoot, Xero and Skinners. Teton Bros is high-functioning outdoor apparel from Japan. ZEAL Optics have a wide selection of high quality sunglasses that are made for being outdoors. Their sunglasses are perfect for any outdoor activity no matter the season. For winter ZEAL has amazing ski goggles that are made for the harshest conditions out there! Next on the Outdoor Gear Guide is Rebecca's Herbal Apothecary & Supply. Stop in to pick up ingredients to make your own sunscreen! They have all the supplies needed to keep you safe from the sun. La Sportiva's brand store showcases the entire lineup of our North America footwear, apparel and accessories for all of your outdoor adventures. Head to prAna for an amazing assortment of hiking and climbing apparel. PrAna's claim to fame is high-performance rock climbing shorts, pants and tops that will withstand the toughest conditions. Their climbing clothing is perfect for a day of hiking, climbing or really any outdoor activity in nature. It wouldn't be an outdoor gear guide without going to North Face. North Face will undoubtedly have what you need for whatever outdoor activity you plan on doing in Boulder. They specialize in making airy shirts, shorts and pants that are all perfect for your next hike or bike ride. North Face also makes a variety of terrific skiwear that will keep you snug in any conditions this winter. Located on the 1100 block of the Pearl Street Mall, Norrøna has you covered for biking, hiking and skiing equipment needs. Norrøna makes awesome lightweight shorts and t-shirts that will definitely take care of any condition you could encounter on the trail. They also have the warmest down jackets and snow-pants that will keep you comfortable even on the coldest and windiest days on the mountain. Cotopaxi creates sustainably designed outdoor gear that fuels both adventure and global change, by dedicating a percentage of their revenues to nonprofits working to improve the human condition. Up next on the outdoor gear guide is Fjällräven. Stop in for a great selection of hiking or climbing apparel and gear. In addition, Fjällräven's amazing backpacks, durable pants and shorts are exactly what you need for your next adventure! Stop in and see new and exciting outdoor brands for a hyper-focused period of time. One brand, the whole shop, every season for you to experience. The first stop on the outdoor gear tour is University Bicycle. The shop has a wide collection of new and used bikes that are available for purchase (or rent). They have bikes for any type of ride- from mountain biking to riding on the street. Not to mention plenty of accessories to keep you comfortable on your next ride!

text: Training for the Nashville St. Paddy’s 5K & Half Marathon with Blisters Training for the Nashville St. Paddy’s Half Marathon & 5K with Blisters We know you are busy training for the upcoming Nashville St. Paddy’s 5K & Half Marathon on March 15th  and we want to keep those feet happy and healthy. As your training ramps up, you might notice new blisters on your toes that were never there before. The freeze-thaw cycle of the Midwest certainly doesn’t help with wet gym shoes as you embark on your training runs. Follow these quick and easy tips to make the best out of your blisters until they go away once and for all: If you already have a blister: Carefully disinfect the blister and Cover it up with a Band-Aid Pro tip: Put some Vaseline on the blisters to it doesn’t stick to the band aid when you take it off (ouch!). Wear the thickest socks that you can find you fit into your shoes The thicker the sock the smaller the chance of your shoe rubbing against your blister or causing another one entirely. We recommend Balega socks as they are specifically padded to prevent rubbing on common blister areas. Soak the Foot in Epsom Salts That will draw the fluid out of the blister and help it to deflate naturally. Wear New Running Shoes Around Your House Then you can be sure how they affect your feet and what they feel like. This will also break them in so your feet don’t cramp and swell on your first long run with the new shoes. The right running socks in your size will completely reduce friction and help circulation and blood flow. Our favorite brands are Balega and Nike. Extra moisture makes the skin softer which makes it easier for a blister to form. Though this can be impossible at the end of winter in the Midwest, try your best to run around puddles instead of through them. If your shoes are too big or too small, they will rub in new places on your feet. This friction will create new blisters and will make it even more difficult to get the shoes back on for a second go-around. Blisters can make running seem impossible and painful, but just know that crossing the finish line in March will make it all worth it! Happy, blister-free, running! Winter Training for a Spring Race Winter Training for A Spring Race Running an outdoor race in March can be tricky, to say the least. One day it might be 65 degrees and the following day you might be freezing cold and rainy. How are we supposed to know what to wear to a race when our weather is so unpredictable at this time of year? There is only one answer: I don’t mean put on 20 shirts like Joey in that episode of though you might trend on Instagram if you do that. Think of yourself as a sandwich, you need layers in order to be your best. This is the layer closest to your body that you will not take off for the duration of the race. Great options are Under Armor, a long-sleeve tec shirt, or if you’re naturally warm blooded, you can even use a tight tank top to do the trick. This layer doesn’t need to break the bank. Check out Kohl’s Tek-Gear line or Old Navy’s workout line if you’re not interested in the more expensive brands. This is the hardest-working layer. It is important that this layer includes some insulation that will contain the heat your body creates while you’re in the race. My favorite mid-layer is my Nike Running vest. It is very thin so it is not heavy, but the thermal insulation keeps my core warm as I move. Another option is to layer a thermal t-shirt over your long-sleeve base layer if you are not . I have incredibly poor circulation in my hands, so the first thing to turn purple on me is my fingers. It puts me in a bad mood and not to mention I can’t use my phone! If you like to change your music/text when you run, be sure to bring gloves with “hot fingers” that allow you to touch your screen. Warm Leggings or Double Leggings. Instead of spending money on wool leggings, I am a big fan of throwing on 2 pairs of sport leggings on cold days. I already have them in my closet and it feels like exact same as wearing a single pair. If you have long hair, check out the hats that have holes in the top for your ponytail. Keeping your head warm will allow most of the heat to be retained by your body and will keep your body and muscles warm as you run. They cost only about $10 at Kohl’s. Ear muffs are another great option but do not offer as much warmth as a hat. It sounds simple, but it is easy to forget that this is a crucial part of staying warm. Be sure to wear longer socks that will cover your ankles from the wind and any precipitation on the ground. If you want to be able to be tagged in those sweet post race photos, make sure you keep your bib on your outermost layer!
